content:
Checking only whether an agent returns a plausible final answer hides subtle failures—such as malformed tool arguments, redundant retries, or silent fallback to outdated assumptions. Step-level trajectory tracing and targeted eval assertions make those failure modes visible before they reach production.
1. Record Every Step in the Execution Trace A useful agent trace captures more than the final text response. Log each turn with enough context to reconstruct what happened and why:
Model decision & reasoning summary: What action or tool call the model chose next. Exact tool input & output payloads: Arguments passed in, responses returned, and execution duration. State & error signals: Non-zero exit codes, schema validation errors, timeouts, or retry counts. 2. Pair Trace Inspection with Deterministic Evals Manual trace inspection helps you spot new failure patterns; automated evals keep fixed bugs from coming back:
Schema and contract assertions: Verify tool arguments match expected types and required fields before execution. Trajectory constraints: Check that critical lookups or verification steps happen rather than being skipped. Regression fixtures: Save real failure traces as test cases so every fix locks in a repeatable check. Key Takeaway Treat agent reliability like systems debugging: inspect the exact step boundary where state or tool output went wrong, then turn that trace into a repeatable eval check.

summary: Why final-answer checks miss broken tool calls, and how step-level tracing and deterministic assertions catch regressions early.
title: Tracing Agent Trajectories and Catching Silent Tool Failures
